subject: Nariway Daily Check-in - 2026-08-20
html:
Nariway Daily Check-in
20 August 2026
 
Needs your attention / action today

Send the Ruth Fine email. Drafted since last Saturday, still unsent five days later — zero cost, ready to go, and Query A’s response window (opened 8/16 eve) closes around 8/23, three days from now, so the window to send it while that outreach’s attention is still live is closing too.

Confirm or pull the Table 1 wealth-manager figure before the report ships. Third consecutive QA audit with this open: the “~51% of wealth managers now offer art services, up from ~25% in 2011” figure is still published as settled despite the claims register’s own note to confirm it — and the report now builds a causal sentence on top of it. Check it against the actual Deloitte Art & Finance report, or pull/caveat the row until you do.
 
Today I learned

A museum can call itself a “Foundation” while carrying far less independent oversight than the name implies. Berlin’s Sammlung Boros markets itself as the “Boros Foundation,” but its actual registered legal form is a gemeinnützige GmbH (a nonprofit LLC), not a German Stiftung — a distinct structure with no equivalent to a Stiftung’s independent supervisory-authority oversight. It matters because “independent governance” is exactly the durability signal the report is built to detect, and this shows a collection can brand that signal without structurally having it. Source note: cases/sammlung-boros.
 
What changed, and what it means

The first wave of conversation outreach is complete. All four people who responded to Query A — Mark Hilbert, Roxanna Zarnegar, Sage Gee, Alexis Hyde — have now been sent five-question replies, the first outward market-facing exchange since Dawn. It is still reach on the Artobiography conversation series, not a test of whether anyone will pay — H7B stays exactly as unproven as it was yesterday.

The case dataset jumped from 54 to 62 in two days, and the ecosystem-research agenda now has a first draft across all 11 chapters — valuation & appraisal was the last untouched stub. The work now shifts from filling gaps to depth (primary-source verification once WebFetch unblocks) and continued breadth toward the ~75/~100 target.

Signals was rebuilt into a genuine daily morning read (orientation, a lead item, grouped sections, a required “worth reading” section), after having gone thin. Worth noticing the difference in tomorrow’s digest.
 
Where we stand

Today was the busiest outward-facing day since Query A launched — four real replies sent, the dataset and ecosystem research both closed real gaps, and the emails now match the brand. But none of it moves the number that matters: still $0 earned, and the one cheap, ready test of whether anyone will pay is the same one that has sat undone since Saturday. The gap between “the machine is working” and “someone has said yes to paying” hasn’t narrowed.
